title: Gabriel Halpern: Grounding and Awakening
description: This practice relates the essence of yoga, as described by the Sutras, to a strong physical practice that addresses the vagus nerve, which controls the parasympathetic nervous system. As you practice, Gabriel also discusses Kundalini, the “spiritual gasoline” that’s said to reside in the base of your spine. When one is awakening the spiritual energies of the body, grounding work with long-held standing and seated poses becomes particularly important for balance.

title: Gabriel Halpern: The Four Basic Movements of the Spine
description: In this practice, Gabriel relates the four movements of the spine, with their physical and energetic effects, to the four varnas, the divisions of society, as mentioned in classical yoga texts. As yoga practitioners, we are called to embody, not only spinal movements, but the different varnas, within ourselves, and ultimately awaken our warrior-like and priestly or wise aspects.

title: Gabriel Halpern: Twists
description: When our minds are calm, we have more space to introspect, reflect, and mull over the nature of reality and the Self, as the Sutras tell us. Through exploring the spiraling energy of the spine in different variations of standing, seating, and supine twists, as well as the relationship between the body and gravity, we work in this practice to move from a more rajasic energy, to more sattvic.

title: Gabriel Halpern: The Levels of Embodied Knowledge
description: In any kind of learning, and particularly embodied learning, one moves from incompetence and the beginner’s ignorance, to increasingly internalized levels of knowledge, in which that knowledge becomes more and more a part of oneself. This strong hatha practice incorporates seated poses, standing poses, and inversions, and focuses on exploring different variations in the poses, and breaking them down into different stages to more fully explore their elements and actions.

title: Gabriel Halpern - Padmasana
description: Gabriel relates Padmasana, lotus pose, to the yogic idea of the five koshas, the five sheaths of the Self or soul, which progress from the physical to the increasingly subtle. This practice contains several prep poses for lotus pose which involve strong external rotation of the hips, such as half lotus, and half pigeon. You can practice this as a 20-minute practice, or, lengthen out the holds in each pose by pausing the video, to make it more yin-like.
